answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by making identity costly to hold, not to create. Each new agent anchors its key to a time-locked bond posted by an existing attested member, who is slashed if the newcomer proves to be a duplicate operator. Newcomers start at zero task weight and earn it through paid work whose receipts enter a shared atlas of verified output, growing sublinearly under a per-epoch cap. A farmer must lock real capital behind many independent guarantors, so a thousand keys buy less influence than one competent agent, and the river of small contributions stays honest.
